assumptions.assumption: the FIFO is built in fabric, not with the FIFO Generator IP.
assumptions.reason: first-word-fall-through over a register read is simplest in plain RTL.

assumptions.assumption: a HEAD read of an empty FIFO is not an error.

behaviour: Depth 16, width 8. LEVEL is the number of bytes stored, 0..16.
A write to PUSH stores wdata[7:0] at the tail when LEVEL < 16; when LEVEL = 16 the byte is dropped, nothing changes and OVERFLOW is set.

Reads are first-word-fall-through: HEAD and POP return the byte at the head now, with no extra read. A read of POP returns the head byte and removes it (LEVEL - 1). A read of HEAD returns the same byte and removes nothing.
A read of POP or HEAD when empty returns 0; a POP read when empty also sets UNDERFLOW. A HEAD read when empty does not.
Bytes leave in the order they arrived, across any number of pointer wraps.
OVERFLOW and UNDERFLOW are sticky: once set they stay set until a write to FLAGS with that bit 1 (write-1-to-clear); a 0 bit leaves its flag alone.
Thermometer - LED[k] = 1 for k < LEVEL, so LEVEL = 16 lights all sixteen and LEVEL = 0 none. No PWM.

tests.text:
"""Acceptance tests of t1_sync_fifo_regs against model.py (hidden from the agent)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import random

import cocotb
from benchmark.lib.bench import Board, peek
from model import AF_THRESH, DESIGN_ID, FLAGS, HEAD, LEVEL, POP, PUSH, Model


class Env:
    def __init__(self, dut) -> None:
        self.b = Board(dut, {})
        self.dut, self.m = dut, Model()

    async def start(self) -> None:
        await self.b.start()

    async def push(self, v: int) -> None:
        await self.b.write(PUSH, v)
        self.m.push(v)

    async def pop(self) -> None:
        want = self.m.pop()
        await self.b.expect(POP, want, "POP")

    async def wr(self, off: int, v: int) -> None:
        await self.b.write(off, v)
        self.m.write(off, v)

    async def check_regs(self) -> None:
        for off, name in ((HEAD, "HEAD"), (LEVEL, "LEVEL"), (FLAGS, "FLAGS"), (AF_THRESH, "AF_THRESH"),
                          (PUSH, "PUSH")):
            await self.b.expect(off, self.m.read(off), name)

    async def check_leds(self) -> None:
        led = await peek(self.b.clk, self.dut.LED)
        assert led == self.m.leds(), f"LED {led:04X} != model {self.m.leds():04X}"


@cocotb.test()
async def test_identity_and_reset(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    assert await e.b.shell_id() == DESIGN_ID
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.check_leds()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_fwft_head_and_pop(dut):
    """Trap: a FIFO Generator in standard (non-FWFT) read mode shows a byte one read late; HEAD and POP here must
    return the head byte at once."""
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.push(0xA1)
    await e.b.expect(HEAD, 0xA1, "HEAD right after the first push")
    await e.push(0xB2)
    await e.push(0xC3)
    await e.b.expect(HEAD, 0xA1, "HEAD")
    await e.pop()                               # A1
    await e.b.expect(HEAD, 0xB2, "HEAD after one pop")
    await e.b.expect(HEAD, 0xB2, "HEAD read twice removes nothing")
    await e.pop()                               # B2
    await e.pop()                               # C3
    await e.pop()                               # empty: 0, UNDERFLOW
    await e.check_regs()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_fill_and_overflow(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    for i in range(16):
        await e.push(0x40 + i)
        if i in (0, 7, 11, 15):
            await e.check_regs()
            await e.check_leds()
    await e.push(0xEE)                          # dropped: OVERFLOW
    await e.push(0xEF)
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.check_leds()
    for _ in range(16):
        await e.pop()
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.check_leds()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_underflow_and_w1c(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.b.expect(HEAD, 0, "HEAD when empty")
    await e.check_regs()                        # a HEAD read when empty is not an underflow
    await e.pop()                               # UNDERFLOW
    for _ in range(17):
        await e.push(7)                         # OVERFLOW too
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.wr(FLAGS, 0)                        # 0 bits clear nothing
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.wr(FLAGS, 1 << 8)                   # clears only OVERFLOW
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.wr(FLAGS, 0x07)                     # read-only bits: ignored
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.wr(FLAGS, 1 << 9)
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.pop()
    await e.wr(FLAGS, 0x300)
    await e.check_regs()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_almost_full_threshold(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    for th in (0, 1, 5, 16, 17, 31, 12):
        await e.wr(AF_THRESH, th)
        await e.check_regs()
    for i in range(16):                         # walk the level with the threshold at 12, then 4
        await e.push(i)
        await e.b.expect(FLAGS, e.m.read(FLAGS), "FLAGS")
    await e.wr(AF_THRESH, 4)
    for _ in range(14):
        await e.pop()
        await e.b.expect(FLAGS, e.m.read(FLAGS), "FLAGS")


@cocotb.test()
async def test_pointer_wrap_order(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    n = 0
    for _ in range(7):                          # level hovers 3..8 while the pointers wrap several times
        for _ in range(8):
            await e.push(n & 0xFF)
            n += 5
        for _ in range(5):
            await e.pop()
        await e.b.expect(LEVEL, e.m.read(LEVEL), "LEVEL")
        await e.b.expect(HEAD, e.m.read(HEAD), "HEAD")
        if len(e.m.q) > 8:
            for _ in range(len(e.m.q) - 3):
                await e.pop()
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.check_leds()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_leds_thermometer(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    for i in range(16):
        await e.push(i)
        await e.check_leds()
    for _ in range(16):
        await e.pop()
        await e.check_leds()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_register_rules(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    await e.push(0x1_2345_6789)                 # only [7:0] stored
    await e.b.write(POP, 0x55)                  # writes to RO registers are ignored (no pop, no push)
    await e.b.write(HEAD, 0x66)
    await e.b.write(LEVEL, 3)
    await e.wr(AF_THRESH, 0xFFFF_FFE3)          # [4:0] only
    await e.check_regs()
    for off in (0x06, 0x41, 0x7F):
        await e.b.expect(off, 0, "unmapped")
    await e.pop()
    await e.check_regs()


@cocotb.test()
async def test_random_traffic(dut):
    e = Env(dut)
    await e.start()
    rng = random.Random(int(cocotb.RANDOM_SEED))
    for _ in range(70):
        r = rng.random()
        bias = 0.6 if len(e.m.q) < 8 else 0.4
        if r < 0.05:
            await e.wr(AF_THRESH, rng.randrange(32))
        elif r < 0.1:
            await e.wr(FLAGS, rng.choice((0x100, 0x200, 0x300)))
        elif r < 0.1 + bias:
            await e.push(rng.getrandbits(8))
        else:
            await e.pop()
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            await e.b.expect(FLAGS, e.m.read(FLAGS), "FLAGS")
    await e.check_regs()
    await e.check_leds()

registers.name: POP

registers.bits: [7:0] head byte, not removed (0 when empty)
registers.name: HEAD

registers.bits: [0] EMPTY, [1] FULL, [2] ALMOST_FULL (read-only); [8] OVERFLOW, [9] UNDERFLOW (sticky, write 1 to clear); other bits 0

interface.unmapped: offsets 0x06-0x7F read 0; writes to them and to RO registers are ignored

requirements.text: HEAD and POP are first-word-fall-through - the first read after a push returns that byte, never a lagged one
Bytes leave in arrival order across pointer wraps; LEVEL and the flags follow the model
Push when full is dropped and sets OVERFLOW; pop when empty returns 0 and sets UNDERFLOW; both are W1C sticky
ALMOST_FULL compares LEVEL >= AF_THRESH for every threshold
The design closes timing at 100 MHz with no unconstrained path
On the board a push/pop sequence over the shell answers as the model predicts

spec_md:
# Byte FIFO behind the test shell

I want a small FIFO on the Nexys A7-100T that I can exercise entirely from the test shell: 16 entries of 8 bits.

- Writing a byte to a push register adds it at the tail. Reading a pop register returns the byte at the head and
  removes it. I also want to look at the head byte without removing it, and to read how many bytes are stored.
- Flags: empty, full, and an almost-full flag whose threshold I can set over the shell.
- Pushing into a full FIFO loses the byte; popping an empty FIFO returns 0. Both mistakes must be remembered in
  sticky error flags until I clear them, each on its own.
- The LEDs show the fill level as a bar graph growing from LED[0].
- CPU_RESETN empties the FIFO and clears every flag.
- The shell runs at 115200 baud on the USB-UART. The design ID is "FIFO".

Test hooks: top module `t1_sync_fifo_regs_top`, ports named as in the board's master XDC, and the test shell's
`CLKS_PER_BIT`, `TIMEOUT_CYCLES` and `BUILD_STAMP` parameters as top-level parameters. There are no other time
constants.
title: Byte FIFO behind the test shell

captions: Op 0: Almost-full threshold set to 4.
Op 1: Push A0: stored, level 0 to 1.
Op 2: Push A1: stored, level 1 to 2.
Op 3: Push A2: stored, level 2 to 3.
Op 4: Push A3: stored, level 3 to 4. Almost-full flag is 1.
Op 5: Push A4: stored, level 4 to 5.
Op 6: Push A5: stored, level 5 to 6.
Op 7: Push A6: stored, level 6 to 7.
Op 8: Push A7: stored, level 7 to 8.
Op 9: Push A8: stored, level 8 to 9.
Op 10: Push A9: stored, level 9 to 10.
Op 11: Push AA: stored, level 10 to 11.
Op 12: Push AB: stored, level 11 to 12.
Op 13: Push AC: stored, level 12 to 13.
Op 14: Push AD: stored, level 13 to 14.
Op 15: Push AE: stored, level 14 to 15.
Op 16: Push AF: stored, level 15 to 16. The FIFO is now full.
Op 17: Push B0: the FIFO is full, so the byte is lost and the overflow flag is set.
Op 18: Read HEAD: A0, the oldest byte, which stays in the FIFO.
Op 19: Pop: returns A0, level 16 to 15.
Op 20: Pop: returns A1, level 15 to 14.
Op 21: Pop: returns A2, level 14 to 13.
Op 22: Pop: returns A3, level 13 to 12.
Op 23: Write FLAGS with 100: the overflow flag is cleared.
Op 24: Pop: returns A4, level 12 to 11.
Op 25: Pop: returns A5, level 11 to 10.
Op 26: Pop: returns A6, level 10 to 9.
Op 27: Pop: returns A7, level 9 to 8.
Op 28: Pop: returns A8, level 8 to 7.
Op 29: Pop: returns A9, level 7 to 6.
Op 30: Pop: returns AA, level 6 to 5.
Op 31: Pop: returns AB, level 5 to 4.
Op 32: Pop: returns AC, level 4 to 3. Almost-full flag is 0.
Op 33: Pop: returns AD, level 3 to 2.
Op 34: Pop: returns AE, level 2 to 1.
Op 35: Pop: returns AF, level 1 to 0. The FIFO is now empty.
Op 36: Pop of an empty FIFO returns 00 and sets the underflow flag.
Op 37: Write FLAGS with 200: the underflow flag is cleared.
trace.stimulus: The almost-full threshold is set to 4. Then 17 bytes are pushed (one more than fits), one is peeked, four are popped, the overflow flag is cleared, the rest are popped, one extra pop hits the empty FIFO and the underflow flag is cleared.

what: A small first-in first-out buffer of sixteen bytes that is driven entirely through the test shell. Writing a byte pushes it on, reading a register removes the oldest byte, and another register lets the user look at the oldest byte without removing it. The design reports empty, full and an almost-full flag with a settable threshold, and keeps sticky error flags for pushing into a full buffer and popping an empty one. The LEDs show the fill level as a bar.
where: FIFOs sit between nearly any two parts of a digital system that run at different rates, such as a UART and a processor, a sensor and a DMA engine, or network packet stages. Almost-full flags are what let a sender slow down in time.
